title: Access matrix brain draft — SOC2 prep (personal scratchpad)
content:
Context / goal:
- Quick personal scratch for access matrix shape we can use for SOC2 evidence sampling. Not an org-deliverable yet — draft for sync with Maya and Rina.
- Scope: console, dedicated admin portal, private control plane, KMS/HSM access, deployment keys for on-prem bundles.

High-level observations (raw):
- Many controls map to "who can rotate keys" / "who can change routing policies" rather than simply 'who can view'. We need to capture both admin privileges and operation-level privileges (deploy, rollback, canary release).
- Evidence artifacts differ by deployment type: hosted API = logs + config snapshots; dedicated = reserved-capacity access records + billing commit; private = local audit trails + HSM audit.

Rough access matrix columns (working):
- Principal (person/group)
- Role (console-admin, infra-operator, customer-support, read-only-audit)
- Privilege type (read, write, execute, approve, rotate)
- Scope (hosted, dedicated, private-VPC, onprem)
- Evidence artifact sample (audit log path / ticket / PR / signed cert)
- Frequency of review (quarterly, semi-annual, ad-hoc)
- Control owner (team/email)

Example rows (hand-sketched):
- "infra-ops@redwood: infra-operator: write,execute: hosted,dedicated: /logs/infra/ops/*.log ; IAM-change PRs (GH#412) ; monthly review: eng-infra"
- "secrets-admin@redwood: keystore-admin: rotate: private-VPC,onprem: HSM-rotation-cert ; KMS audit entries ; quarterly: security"
- "support-ledger@redwood: customer-support: read: hosted: support-activity-export-YYYY-MM.csv ; ephemeral tokens only ; monthly: customer-success"

Open questions (to resolve before handing to compliance):
1) How do we classify "can start a dedicated cluster" vs "can scale it"? Are they separate privileges or the same role?
2) Are deployment keys for on-prem bundles ephemeral per-release or long-lived? Evidence expectation from auditor will differ.
3) For Private (VPC) customers, what is our visibility requirement? Do we need to store a copy of the audit trail off-customer network for SOC2 evidence? (privacy/legal tradeoff)
4) Where does "automatic fallback routing" live in the matrix? Is it a config owned by runtime or by platform? Need an owner.

Quick TODOs (actions I will take):
- [ ] Turn example rows into CSV exportable format: columns above. (Q: should reviewer see sample CSV?)
- [ ] Pull KMS/HSM rotation log samples and anonymize for evidence folder (see Confluence link). Ticket: JIRA-TRUST-1289 assigned to Maya.
- [ ] Schedule 30m sync with Rina to align owners for canary/rollback privileges (propose Tue 3/9).
- [ ] Create ephemeral key guidance doc for on-prem packaging (start draft in GH).

Quick heuristics for evidence sampling (my brain dump):
- If privilege can effect customer data access (eg: snapshot restore, KV export), require 2 independent artifacts: PR/Change record + signed log entry within 24 hours.
- For high-risk operations (key rotation, HSM config), prefer HSM-signed certs and ticket number in commit message.
- For role changes: combine IAM change log + email approval thread (Slack convo is fine if thread permalink included).

Notes to self:
- Don't forget to link the rollout policy docs (product/console) — they show who can configure "fallback" behavior.
- Ask SRE about log retention for dedicated pools (current retention 90 days for error-level, 30 for debug — auditor may want 12 months).

Draft mapping snippet (copy/paste ready, still manual):
Principal|Role|Privilege|Scope|Evidence sample|Review cadence|Owner
infra-ops@redwood|infra-operator|create/scale/destroy|dedicated,hosted|GHPR#412 + /logs/infra/ops/2026-02-xx.log|monthly|eng-infra
keystore-admin@security|keystore-admin|rotate|private-VPC,onprem|HSM-audit-2026-02-12.pdf;KMS-CloudTrail|quarterly|security
support@cs|support-read|read-tenant-metadata|support-export-2026-01.csv|monthly|customer-success

Conversation snippets to capture (for context):
- Slack: <https://redwood.slack.com/archives/C0TRUST/p1676000000000> — discussion on "who can create dedicated clusters" (has a few decisions we can cite).
- Confluence: Access Matrix template (to copy into final) - page under TRUST.

Lower-priority thoughts (floating):
- Could we model 'capability flags' as short TTL tokens for operational tasks so records are shorter-lived and easier to sample? (tradeoff: complexity vs auditability)
- Consider building a small AWS Lambda to auto-collect evidence artifacts for a given JIRA ticket id (collect relevant logs, PRs, and emails). Prototype = low priority but nice-to-have.

Draft hand-off checklist for compliance reviewer (what I will provide):
- CSV export of access matrix with sample anonymized artifacts (one per high-risk privilege)
- Folder with screenshots of console ACL pages + corresponding GHPR or ticket
- KMS/HSM rotation proof (anonymized)
- Short written rationale for owners and review cadence per role

Immediate next steps (this week):
- Transform rows into CSV and drop into /private/trust-drafts/access-matrix-2026/ (Maya to confirm path)
- Collect 2 anonymized HSM rotation records from security team
- Queue a meeting with Rina and Eng-Infra for owner alignment

Random personal TODOs (meta):
- If this becomes the canonical template, add a small sample script to generate the CSV from IAM logs (python).
- Keep this doc as 'scratch' until Maya marks it 'ready-for-review' then move to Confluence.

End of scratch — will tidy after syncs.

-- Quentin
